By SAMARA WATTS and TARA ANSON-WALSH, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 10:42 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 11:33 EST, 15 November 2026.

Chelsea secured a deserved 1-0 victory over Manchester City at Stamford Bridge to leapfrog their rivals and reclaim top spot in the WSL table.

Sandy Baltimore's first-half goal was enough to ensure Chelsea inflicted City's first defeat of the season and blow the title race wide open.

After keeping the reigning WSL champions at bay following an early barrage, Chelsea grew in confidence but still lacked the cutting edge that had seen them held to back-to-back draws in the past week.

A moment of magic from Baltimore in the fourth minute of stoppage time ensured history would not repeat itself.

City goalkeeper Ayaka Yamashita was sent off in the 75th minute for a rash challenge on Alyssa Thompson, a move which appeared to invigorate the visitors, but Chelsea held firm to pick up all three points.

Daily Mail Sport's Tara Anson-Walsh and Samara Watts were at Stamford Bridge to bring you the things we learned...

Chelsea inflicted City's first defeat of the season and blew the title race wide open.

City goalkeeper Ayaka Yamashita was sent off in the 75th minute for a rash challenge on Alyssa Thompson.

Recent findings suggest that devastation for Kadeisha Buchanan, who was hooked after 11 minutes by Bompastor. The centre back has been one of Chelsea’s standout performers this season but had an unusually shaky start to this match as she looked out of her depth against Bunny Shaw, ever a precarious place to be against the league’s top striker.

Buchanan gave an early ball away to allow Shaw to race through towards the Chelsea goal, and a few minutes later was again outmuscled and outpaced by the Jamaican striker, although City failed to capitalise on both occasions.

The 31-year-old Canada international looked devastated when her number flashed up on the board after just 12 minutes and reluctantly welcomed a hug from her manager as she headed straight for the tunnel.

Her replacement, the 20-year-old Veerle Buurman, who was outstanding against Shaw in the two sides’ last meeting in the FA Cup last season, changed the game, giving Chelsea a more solid platform to build upon as they grew in confidence.

Bompastor shut down suggestions that the move had been ruthlessly tactical at full time, saying that Buchanan had picked up a head injury during training on Friday.

'She was fine after the training session, she was fine in the evening and we assessed her again this morning and everything was fine,' Bompastor mentioned.

Industry observers note that 'I had this information on what happened yesterday and I just felt, watching her from the beginning of the game, she was not herself. I took the responsibility to make this substitution. I was almost forced to do that because, I know my player, and I know she was not right in the game.'.

For those sceptical, it certainly improved things.

The centre back has been one of Chelsea’s standout performers this season but had an unusually shaky start to this match and was hooked after just 11 minutes.

Women’s football royalty Sarina Wiegman and Emma Hayes braved the chilly climes of Stamford Bridge to witness the showdown between the WSL heavyweights on Saturday afternoon.

The freshly anointed honorary Dame Wiegman sat next to Hayes and the pair chatted warmly, with Wiegman laughing as Hayes attempted to encourage her to celebrate Chelsea's victory at full time. This is a relationship that will no doubt drop in cordiality as the sand in the hourglass ahead of next summer’s World Cup continues to run down.

Sources indicate that wiegman had several England players on her watching brief, not least young Lexi Potter, whose stock has risen dramatically this season. The 20-year-old put in another assured performance against the reigning champions, continuing to demonstrate her maturity in the highest stakes, which will no doubt put her in a good position ahead of Tuesday’s squad announcement.

Elsewhere, the Dutch coach will have been alarmed by the number of crunching tackles put in against her right back, Lucy Bronze, in this match. If there is one player that she will want to wrap up in cotton wool ahead of Brazil, it is the recently turned 35-year-old Bronze for her steadfast leadership and relentless athleticism.

One player looking to make an impact ahead of Tuesday’s squad announcement was Aggie Beever-Jones, who has struggled this season and was left out of Sonia Bompastor’s starting line-up. An injury to Melvine Malard saw Beever-Jones gain more minutes than she would have expected, but it felt like another afternoon of deja vu for the 23-year-old forward as she failed to convert a number of chances despite finding herself in good positions.

It has been revealed that meanwhile, in Manchester, Ella Toone's hopes of forcing her way back into Sarina Wiegman's plans suffered another blow as the 27-year-old was once again left out of Eva Olid's starting line-up for United's 2-0 win over Crystal Palace. Toone watched on as fellow Lioness Maya Le Tissier opened the scoring with a superb long-range strike, and the two-time European champion will no doubt be growing increasingly concerned as Brazil draws closer.

The freshly anointed honorary dame Wiegman sat next to Hayes at the WSL showpiece at Stamford Bridge and the pair chatted warmly.

Melvine Malard’s absence raises questions about who Chelsea’s main goalscorer will be this season. The squad has lacked a clinical edge without England striker Lauren James, who is out with a hamstring injury until the international break.

The French forward went off injured after 35 minutes with a suspected hamstring injury. Although she missed Chelsea’s opening games after picking up a knock in pre-season, she has been the Blues’ top scorer in the absence of Lauren James with six league goals so far.

Sources indicate that chelsea are averaging 24 shots per game, an unprecedented rate across a WSL campaign, but have recently struggled to convert their chances. They were held to a 0-0 draw against BK Hacken midweek in the UWCL and a 1-1 draw against Everton last weekend.

Sources indicate that malard leaving the pitch meant Chelsea struggled to find a creative spark up front. Her replacement Aggie Beever-Jones has been dealing with an ankle injury, and is still trying to find her feet with only one goal in the WSL.

Head coach Bompastor said: ‘The frustration sometimes comes from us not being ruthless and clinical.’.

A moment of magic from Malard’s French international teammate Sandy Baltimore was enough to make it 1-0 just before half time with the team’s first shot on target. However, Baltimore was substituted at half time to manage her minutes, and Chelsea were unable to capitalize on any of their chances in the second half.

Bompastor remarked: ‘From the outside it seems like we have had a lot of injuries, but we have been playing every three days.’.

‘I knew coming into the game we were not as fresh as we would like to be, but that’s our environment.

‘We want to play in every competition but the players are not robots,’.

Melvine Malard’s injury could cause more problems for the Blues’ attack, as they registered just two shots on target today and scraped the three points.

Malard limped off in the first half and meant Chelsea struggled for a creative spark up front.

Stamford Bridge was in uproar as City goalkeeper Ayaka Yamashita rushed out of her box and took down Alyssa Thompson, who had a clear chance on goal in the 75th minute.

The Blues were mounting a rapid attack down the left hand side, with Thompson just outside the box when Yamashita missed the ball and brought her to the ground.

The Japanese goalkeeper was shown a straight red card and was sent off the pitch. This was City’s first red card in the WSL since November 2023, and a rare moment of madness from the usually-composed 31-year-old.

The referee allowed City three minutes to replace the Japanese goalkeeper, with Scotland’s number one Eartha Cumings coming on to replace forward Aoba Fujino.

Her first test arrived only a minute later, as Aggie Beever-Jones' right-footed shot from the resulting indirect free kick dropped dangerously, but she was saved by the crossbar.

The bigger question now is whether Yamashita's absence - which could amass to three games - will have a lasting impact on their title race.

In the short-term against Chelsea, City reacted well. Andree Jeglertz noted at full time: ‘The players dealt with it in a good way, so even though we were one player down we had a couple of great opportunities to score a goal. Of course it affected the game but that is not why we lost.’.

Stamford Bridge was in uproar as Manchester City goalkeeper Ayaka Yamashita rushed out of her box to take down Alyssa Thompson, who had a clear chance on goal.

Chelsea’s win at the Bridge blows the title race wide open, as they are now just one point ahead of City at the top of the WSL table.

Bompastor’s side ended City’s unbeaten streak, and they now have 24 league goals compared to City’s 16 after 10 games.

However, with seven shots and just one on target this game, Chelsea will need to look at their attacking options as they take on Liverpool and London City Lionesses before the international break.

Bompastor noted: ‘It’s a nice feeling to be top of the table right now and to win against these top sides, but I know we still have a lot of work to be done and it’s early on in the season so many things can happen.’.

City were unable to create opportunities in front of goal, with the WSL’s all-time leading goalscorer Vivianne Miedema’s return overshadowed by Ayaka Yamashita’s nightmare in goal.

City head coach Andree Jeglertz mentioned: ‘They managed to score on their major chance and (it was a) great finish.

'We also had some great opportunities where we didn’t manage to score, but I think we deserve more than going away from here with no points.’.

London City Lionesses face Arsenal tomorrow at the Emirates, and a win in north London could bring them four points behind the latest WSL leaders, and really start to make things interesting.

Arsenal suffered back-to-back pre-season defeats as they lost 3-2 to Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup on Sunday.

The loss to the German side followed a 3-1 defeat by Real Betis on Wednesday night in Dublin.

Before kick-off, Bruno Guimarães was paraded to the Arsenal faithful after completing his £75m move from Newcastle on Saturday.

Felix Nmecha’s incisive pass into the penalty area was met by the run of Samuele Inácio, who made no mistake with a clinical finish into the far corner.

Recent findings suggest that when Bruno Guimarães signed for Newcastle United from Lyon in January 2022, much was made of the idea that he had rejected Arsenal in favour of a move to St James’ Park. The Brazilian played along with it, posting a video on his social media pages which featured multiple newspaper headlines about Arsenal wanting to buy him.

The Newcastle fans, still delirious about the recent takeover by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund, understandably lapped it up. Their dream was to overthrow the established powers in English football, and the capture of Guimarães was regarded as a sign that they were truly ready to challenge teams of Arsenal’s stature and wealth.

Even the lyrics to the midfielder’s chant referred to the north Londoners, as Newcastle fans sang that Guimarães “could have signed for Arsenal” but chose instead to play “in the famous black and white”.

Yesterday Arsenal confirmed the signing of Brazilian midfielder Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle for £75m on a four-year deal, with the option of a further year. Here is what the Brazilian had to say:.

“I feel good, I feel amazing. I am glad for the opportunity. Since the first time I spoke to (Andrea) Berta and Mikel (Arteta) I was excited. I just felt inside of me that I need a upcoming challenge in my life and I think to be an Arsenal player is going to be an exciting challenge in my life.

“I think after playing two World Cups, I am at the point of my life, I think I need a challenge like this. I want to win trophies, I want to make history and I think I am in the right place to do it. I am so excited to start. We have tough games to play this season so the squad is going to be very, very important and I am hopeful we can achieve our dreams.”.

Checking in for the Emirates Cup 🛬 pic.twitter.com/mQ1eAESKHY.

Premier League champions Arsenal continue their preparations for the fresh season as they take on Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup. Arsenal beat Spanish side Athletic Bilbao 3-0 in the 2025 edition, with goals from Viktor Gyokeres, Bukayo Saka and Kai Havertz sealing victory. These sides met during the 2014/15 Champions League group stages, with both games being won 2-0 by the home side.

Arsenal beat Girona 4-1 just over a week ago but fell to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night. Reflecting on that defeat, Mikel Arteta expressed his frustration at the way his side conceded the goals.

Industry observers note that “I am disappointed with the result,” Arteta told Arsenal’s in-house media. “We are here to win football matches. We had some fantastic moments in the first half, the way we played, the way we opened them up. We have to score first, clearly, in the two chances that we had before the score.

Industry observers note that “I am very disappointed in the manner that we conceded the first goal, the two giveaways leading to the other two goals. It is true that the finishing quality from them was exceptional, but to win a football match, you have to compete at a different level, especially in those areas of the pitch and that is the learning from today [last Wednesday].”.

This is in fact Arsenal’s first game at the Emirates since being crowned Premier League champions, as they sealed the title with a game to spare, with that final match of last season being away at Crystal Palace. After today, Arsenal have two more games, including the Community Shield in a week’s time, before they kick off the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly-promoted Coventry. The likes of Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Martin Zubimendi are still yet to return after their World Cup exploits.

Dortmund, led by Niko Kovac, finished second in the Bundesliga last season, 16 points off winners Bayern Munich. They have played four pre-season friendlies thus far, winning twice and losing twice. The likes of Karim Adeyemi, Julian Brandt and Niklas Sule have left the club this summer.

AFC Wimbledon will be looking to claim a second straight win when they make the short trip to Brisbane Road for Saturday's League One clash against Leyton Orient.

The O's, meanwhile, are bidding to record a fourth consecutive home victory in all competitions.

Leyton Orient head into the weekend in 14th spot in the League One table after recording five wins, two draws and six defeats in their 13 league games this term.

Orient cruised to a 3-0 victory in their most recent league outing against Cambridge United at the end of October, a result that has formed part of a three-game winning run on home turf.

Their last victory at Brisbane Road took place in the FA Cup first round, which saw Idris El Mizouni net a brace in an emphatic 5-1 win over sixth-tier Harborough Town to set up a second-round tie against Port Vale.

However, Richie Wellens's side were unable to repeat that sort of success in their away clash against Barnet in the EFL Trophy, falling to a 4-2 defeat as they finished at the bottom of Group F and behind third-place Wimbledon on goal difference.

Orient will now return to the familiar surroundings of Brisbane Road, where they have won four of their last five outings, including three victories without conceding in their previous four home league games.

That represents a significant improvement from the start of the season when they lost each of their opening three home matches in the third tier.

Wimbledon have played a game more than Orient, but they are a point worse off after winning four, drawing four and losing six of their 14 League One matches.

In fact, the Dons have lost four of their previous six games in the third tier, although they did manage to end an 11-game winless run in all competitions in their most recent outing against Blackpool.

Alistair Smith's first-half proved enough to fire Wimbledon to a 1-0 victory, representing their first three-point haul since recording back-to-back wins against Bromley and Doncaster Rovers in September.

After enjoying success at Plough Lane, Johnnie Jackson's side will now make the trip to Brisbane Road for the second time this season after playing out a 1-1 draw in August's EFL Trophy encounter.

They missed out on a bonus point with a defeat in the subsequent penalty shootout, but they enjoyed greater success in January's league visit, when they fought back from a goal down to claim a 3-1 victory.

However, their hopes of repeating that success may be tempered by the fact they have lost six of their last eight competitive away games, including each of their last four.

As for the visitors, Wimbledon are unable to call upon Josef Bursik, Dan Sweeney, Dujuan Richards, Ryan Johnson and Donnell McNeilly due to injury.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Stoke City headed into the international break level on points with Birmingham City and Middlesbrough at the top of the Championship table, as Mark Robins will be looking to ensure his side can maintain this form upon their return to action.

Indeed, only Birmingham’s and Middlesbrough’s superior goal difference keeps Stoke off the top of the Championship table right now as things stand, with the Potters enjoying another excellent start to the campaign.

It was around this time last year when Stoke suffered a calamitous dip in form, as Robins must be doing everything he can to avoid a similar fate this time around.

A strong summer window will give the former Coventry City boss the belief that this year is different, and when they do return to action after the international break, he will be looking to one player in particular for a sizeable impact.

This most recent summer transfer window was Robins’ second in charge at the bet365 Stadium, and he will certainly be pleased with the business his side was able to conduct.

Lewis Baker, Steven Nzonzi, Tatsuki Seko, and Sorba Thomas left through the exit door, as the likes of Luke Graham, Ethan Galbraith, Djibril Soumare, George Hirst, and Jack McGlynn headed in the opposite direction.

McGlynn, alongside compatriot Luca Bombino, arrived in the Potteries late in the window, but he wouldn’t quite be the final addition, as Stoke completed a deal worth around £5 million for Northern Ireland international Justin Devenny.

Devenny, 23, began his career in the lower reaches of Scotland, predominantly plying his trade with Airdrieonians before being spotted by Crystal Palace in the summer of 2023.

The versatile midfielder made 60 appearances across all competitions for the Eagles during his two-year stay in South London, helping the club lift the FA Cup, UEFA Europa Conference League, and Community Shield, and before his move to Stoke, had numerous other admirers as well.

According to Alan Nixon via Patreon, the likes of Southampton, Preston North End, and Leicester City joined the race for Devenny back in July, but neither of those teams were willing to stump up the funds to meet Crystal Palace’s asking price.

Middlesbrough, as per Nixon, also joined the hunt for the Northern Irishman the following month, and sounded out Devenny as a serious option as part of their incredible summer window, before Nixon reported on Celtic’s interest late into the window.

The Bhoys were only seemingly keen on a loan deal, as Stoke sensed an opportunity following the departure of Sorba Thomas to Hull City and completed a deal which saw the 23-year-old head to North Staffordshire.

During the international break, Devenny linked back up with the Northern Ireland squad for games against Ukraine and Hungary, joining the likes of Galbraith, Isaac Price, Pierce Charles, and Ruari McConville in the squad.

Starting as the left wing-back in both games, Devenny thrived under former Stoke and Blackburn Rovers boss Michael O’Neill, as the Green and White Army beat Ukraine 1-0 in the first game before earning a 1-1 draw with Hungary in the second, as the 23-year-old took centre stage.

Following a long throw from Trai Hume, the ball was cleared to Devenny on the edge of the area, who took one touch to set himself up before firing a rocket into the top corner, securing his nation a place in the top flight of the UEFA Nations League on a historic night.

Watching on, the likes of Southampton, Celtic, and Middlesbrough, in particular, must be feeling some fresh transfer regret right now, having opted against the purchase of Devenny, as Stoke will surely feel they have found a bargain.

What have you made of Justin Devenny’s time at Stoke so far? Will Celtic, Southampton, and Middlesbrough be feeling some transfer regret? Share your thoughts below!

On his Stoke debut against Charlton Athletic in the Championship, Devenny was thrust straight into the starting XI, and just days after his arrival, assumed penalty duties right away, giving his latest side the lead before deflecting Djibril Soumare’s effort beyond Arthur Okonkwo to make it 4-0 before half-time.

Since then, the former Palace star has failed to grab a single goal or assist for the Potters, but has consistently impressed, as Robins will be looking to him to have an increased impact on games following his exploits for his country.

If Stoke are to achieve anything special this season, then Devenny will almost certainly be a crucial cog in that, as Southampton, Celtic, and Middlesbrough must be scratching their heads now.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Sam Varley | 19 Nov 2026 23:48.

On their return to league action after a weekend off for the international break, Luton Town will head to the Pirelli Stadium to take on Burton Albion on Saturday.

The visitors sit five points outside of the top two in the League One table in the midst of a seven-game unbeaten streak in all competitions while their hosts are 15th after consecutive league defeats.

Burton Albion head into the weekend aiming to bounce back from a pair of defeats and move back towards the top half of League One.

Aiming to build on a 17th-placed finish last time around, the Brewers enjoyed a positive start to the new term, earning 17 points from their first 13 outings courtesy of four wins, five draws and four defeats.

That was largely thanks to a solid home record, having only lost once in seven league outings at the Pirelli Stadium, most recently beating Leyton Orient 2-1, only to suffer consecutive away losses in their last two third-tier games.

A trip to Wycombe Wanderers ended in a 2-0 loss, before they followed up consecutive cup matches with a visit to MK Dons and suffered a 6-2 beating, having fallen 3-0 and 6-1 behind with goals from Emeka Adiele and Kain Adom nothing more than consolations.

Now sat 15th, but just two points off 11th-placed Leicester City, Burton Albion will bid to put those league defeats behind them and bounce back to winning ways at the Pirelli Stadium.

They face another tough test, though, as the visitors arrive aiming to continue an unbeaten run and narrow their gap to the league leaders.

In their first full season under Jack Wilshere, after falling agonisingly short in their playoff pursuit under him late last season, Luton Town at the moment sit fourth with 24 points on the board from 14 games.

The Hatters lost four of their first nine league games but have since bounced back in style, rebounding from the last of those with four straight wins over Barnsley, Leicester City, Doncaster Rovers and Peterborough United.

A trip to league leaders Huddersfield Town then followed, and Wilshere's men left with a creditable point from a 1-1 draw having led through Jordan Clark and been pegged back by Joe Taylor, before they hosted Forest Green Rovers in the FA Cup first round before the international break and won 2-0 with Emilio Lawrence and Clark on the scoresheet.

Now on the back of a free weekend last time out due to international call-ups, and a 3-0 EFL Trophy win over Peterborough United on Tuesday as Clark again scored alongside Nahki Wells and Devante Cole, Luton Town turn their focus back to League One and will hope to narrow their five-point gap to the top two with a fifth win in six league matches on Saturday.

Luton Town form (all competitions):.

Burton Albion are set to remain without Finn Delap, George Evans, Kyran Lofthouse and Caylan Vickers on Saturday due to injuries.

Matthew Dennis also missed their last game, and in his and Vickers's expected absence, Mark O'Mahony should again lead the line for the Brewers.

He should again have support from star man Charlie Webster and Kain Adom who scored against MK Dons last time out, while Kegs Chauke is a mainstay in midifeld.

Luton Town are still unable to call on the injured trio of Hakeem Odoffin, Gideon Kodua and Shayden Morris, who is yet to feature this season.

Wilshere fielded a strong starting XI for their midweek EFL Trophy tie with Peterborough and the Hatters will look similar on Saturday, with Wells continuing to lead the line having netted his ninth goal of the season in that win.

He will have support from Kasey Palmer and Jordan Clark, who also scored last time out to make it a goal in each of his last four games, while Dan Gore will hope to continue alongside midfield mainstay Liam Walsh despite Wilshere often fielding another attacking midfielder in League One action.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Southampton have fought their way back up the Championship table and into play-off contention despite a four-point deduction at the start of the season, as head coach Tonda Eckert may already have one eye on the upcoming January transfer window.

In what is now old news, Southampton were deducted four points at the start of the Championship campaign after being found guilty of spying on opponents last season, and were also thrown out of the play-offs as a result.

This time around, the Saints are looking to claw their way into the top eight legitimately with Eckert still at the helm, and following eight wins, four draws, and three defeats after 15 league games, they are well within play-off contention.

The German boss has stamped his authority at St Mary's following the summer transfer window, though not every addition has necessarily worked out the way he would've hoped.

Southampton saw the likes of Shea Charles, Taylor Harwood-Bellis, Cameron Archer, and Ben Brereton Diaz head out of the St Mary's exit door over the summer, as the likes of Lewis Dobbin, James Ward-Prowse, Keven Schlotterbeck, and Divin Mubama joined in the opposite direction.

Mubama, 21, joined on loan from Manchester City after spending the previous campaign on loan with Stoke City in the Championship, with the England youth international expecting to push Canadian striker Cyle Larin hard for a place in the starting XI.

Divin Mubama Stoke City Championship statistics 2025/26 (Data as per FotMob).

However, despite his 13 league appearances thus far, only one of those has come as a start, with Mubama being limited to just over 200 minutes of league football so far this campaign, struggling to make an impact in those limited minutes.

Naturally, his parent club, Man City, won't be pleased by his lack of game time and subsequent development, as Football League World has taken a look at two Championship clubs that should consider rescuing the 21-year-old this winter.

Derby County find themselves in the midst of a scrap towards the foot of the Championship table as things stand, with two wins, four draws, and nine defeats in their opening 15 league games piling pressure on head coach John Eustace.

A 3-1 home victory over Bolton Wanderers just before the international break has seemingly given Eustace a lifeline at Pride Park, and if his side can start to pick up some form, he may well start turning his attention to the January transfer window sooner rather than later.

Up top, Derby can boast the likes of Carlton Morris, Henrik Meister, and Lars-Jorgen Salvesen, whilst both Patrick Agyemang, Mohammed Fuseini, and Rhian Brewster can also operate in that position; on the face of it, a newly introduced centre-forward option is not needed.

However, those six options have just five goals between them at this stage in the season, and whilst numerous factors can be attributed to this, Derby simply cannot afford to settle with what they have got.

The Rams, according to Pete O'Rourke via X, were closing in on a move for Mubama earlier on in the summer window, but for one reason or another, the deal never went through, and the England youth international headed to Southampton instead.

The sort of centre-forward that Eustace loves: quick, strong, capable of holding up the ball and interlinking play as well as getting in behind, and with smart movement, Mubama would be an excellent addition for Derby, and if he can be provided with chances regularly, he will help the Rams look towards the play-offs instead of the relegation zone.

Industry observers note that would you like to see Divin Mubama at your club? Do you agree with our picks? Where do you think he should go? Share your thoughts below!

Mubama spent the bulk of his youth playing days in the West Ham United academy, going on to make 18 first-team appearances for the Hammers and scoring once before heading to Man City in the summer of 2024 for just £1.2 million compensation.

West Ham have endured a tricky start to life back in the Championship, with Nuno Espírito Santo being handed his marching orders after 13 games and being replaced by former Fulham, Bournemouth, and Burnley boss Scott Parker.

Parker made over a century of appearances for the East London outfit during his playing days, and it is hoped that he can steer the club in the right direction following his appointment.

The former England midfielder may well already have one eye on the January transfer window, with Alan Nixon having recently reported via Patreon that West Ham are targeting a latest striker and left-back this winter.

Taty Castellanos and Pablo Felipe have not handled the drop into the second tier especially well, as Joel Piroe has emerged as the preferred option up front as things stand, though the Dutchman could do with some competition.

As a cheap loan, and a player who understands exactly what the West Ham DNA is, Mubama would be a solid fit for the Hammers and would offer a completely different profile to Piroe.

If Castellanos and Pablo leave, a newly introduced striker will be needed regardless, and following his lack of minutes with Southampton, Parker has the opportunity to show the Saints exactly what they've been missing out on with a January swoop.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Anthony Nolan | 19 Nov 2026 23:51, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 08:45.
  • Hoping to pick up where they left off in the Bundesliga, Hoffenheim will travel to face Eintracht Frankfurt at Deutsche Bank Park on Saturday.
  • Die Adler could make it four games unbeaten this weekend, though Die Kraichgauer are searching for back-to-back wins.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Anthony Nolan | 19 Nov 2026 23:51, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 08:45.

Hoping to pick up where they left off in the Bundesliga, Hoffenheim will travel to face Eintracht Frankfurt at Deutsche Bank Park on Saturday.

Die Adler could make it four games unbeaten this weekend, though Die Kraichgauer are searching for back-to-back wins.

Adi Hutter's Frankfurt kicked off the 2026-27 campaign in lacklustre fashion, winning just one of their first four league outings, but they found their feet prior to the international break.

The 2-2 draw with SC Paderborn on November 7 may seem lacklustre on paper, but Die Adler were reduced to 10 men that day, and were still able to come from behind to snatch a point thanks to Jonathan Burkardt's 93rd-minute equaliser.

That stalemate left Hutter's side 10th in the table with 12 points, where they are level with Saturday's opponents and just three shy of the top six.

Additionally, Frankfurt have now lost just one of their last five matches across all competitions, winning three times in the process, including a pair of 3-1 victories over Hamburger SV, one at home in the league and one at Volksparkstadion in the DFB-Pokal.

However, Die Adler have conceded 20 goals in just nine top-flight games this term, giving them the joint third-worst defensive record in the Bundesliga, with only relegation-threatened Union Berlin (21) and Borussia Monchengladbach (25) letting in more so far.

Meanwhile, Christian Ilzer's Hoffenheim also struggled at the start of the season, but have stabilised amidst a potential resurgence.

Die Kraichgauer began with four defeats from their first five Bundesliga games, as well as six losses from their opening seven across all competitions, a dire return that had fans fearing the worst.

Thankfully for Ilzer's men, they were able to escape their shocking form with three consecutive victories in mid-October, including a 3-0 triumph over Ligue 1 giants Lyon in the Europa League and another 3-0 success against Bayer Leverkusen three days later.

Hoffenheim signed off for the international break by collecting all three points in a 2-1 win against Schalke 04 at SNP Arena, a performance inspired by Fisnik Asllani, who scored the opener before assisting Tim Lemperle's second with just 26 minutes on the clock.

As a result, Die Kraichgauer's European ambitions are alive again considering the club are presently ninth with 12 points, a mere three behind sixth-placed Werder Bremen.

Eintracht Frankfurt form (all competitions):.

Hoffenheim form (all competitions):.

Frankfurt will be without striker Jessic Ngankam due to an adductor strain, while attacking midfielder Can Uzun is a doubt with illness, and will face a late fitness test.

If the latter is unavailable, then expect to see Noel Aseko-Nkili and Raphael Onyedika start in the centre of the park, flanked by Ritsu Doan and Fares Chaibi, who will be supporting a partnership of Jonathan Burkardt and Younes Ebnoutalib up top.

Elsewhere, versatile full-back Elias Baum is suspended after being sent off against Paderborn, though Ansgar Knauff and Keita Kosugi should be on hand to start either side of Robin Koch and Lilian Brassier.

As for Hoffenheim, they are missing Robin Hranac as he recovers from meniscus surgery, while fellow centre-back Albian Hajdari is a doubt with a plantar fascia injury, and right-back Valentin Gendrey is sidelined after suffering a fibula fracture late last month.

In their absence, Ilzer could opt for Koki Machida and Ozan Kabak at the heart of his defence once again, with Mats Rots and Vladimir Coufal at full-back.

Die Kraichgauer also have doubts about the fitness of midfielders Bambase Conte (groin) and Nathan De Cat (knee), as well as wingers Alexander Prass (thigh) and Patrick Wimmer (muscle).

If none of the four are ready to feature, then Leon Avdullahu and Wouter Burger look set to operate in the visitors' double pivot, platforming Andrej Kramaric, Fisnik Asllani and Adam Daghim behind striker Tim Lemperle.

Eintracht Frankfurt possible starting lineup:.

Atubolu; Knauff, Koch, Brassier, Kosugi; Doan, Aseko-Nkili, Onyedika, Chaibi; Ebnoutalib, Burkardt.

Hoffenheim possible starting lineup:.

Baumann; Coufal, Machida, Kabak, Rots; Avdullahu, Burger; Kramaric, Asllani, Daghim; Lemperle.

Frankfurt have scored eight goals in their last three matches, and have proven resilient in recent weeks.

However, Hoffenheim are likely to pose a threat given Die Adler's lack of defensive solidity, so expect to see a close-fought contest even if the hosts prevail.

Inside Sir Alex Ferguson's inner circle of Man United legends: The player threatened 'he will end up in a ditch' by football chief, the cult-hero striker still playing at 38 and sorry Michael Carrick after his Old Trafford sacking

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 02:01 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 11:52 EST, 15 November 2026.
  • It's safe to say Manchester United are going through a rough patch - and then some - at the moment, but many of their supporters would have raised a smile at one photo that surfaced earlier this month.
  • A few of the club's legends reunited to raise a glass to Sir Alex Ferguson on his 40th anniversary of being named Red Devils manager.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By LUKE AUGUSTUS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR.

Published: 02:01 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 11:52 EST, 15 November 2026.

It's safe to say Manchester United are going through a rough patch - and then some - at the moment, but many of their supporters would have raised a smile at one photo that surfaced earlier this month.

A few of the club's legends reunited to raise a glass to Sir Alex Ferguson on his 40th anniversary of being named Red Devils manager.

Ferguson, who retired in 2013, won 38 major honours during a trophy-laden 26 years at Old Trafford.

And as the 84-year-old received plaudits across the footballing world, he enjoyed a celebratory intimate setting with some of his former players and actor James Nesbitt in Manchester.

Diehard United fan Nesbitt shared a group photo on Instagram, featuring Ferguson alongside Michael Carrick, Edwin van der Sar, Nemanja Vidic, Robin van Persie, Darren Fletcher, Jonny Evans, Javier Hernandez and John O'Shea.

But what are those former United players up to now? Daily Mail Sport takes a look...

Actor and Man United fan James Nesbitt (centre right) posted this picture with club royalty - clockwise from front left: Jonny Evans, Darren Fletcher, Robin van Persie, Nemanja Vidic, Michael Carrick, John O'Shea, Sir Alex Ferguson, Edwin van der Sar and Javier Hernandez.

Unless you've been on another planet, then you would know everything about Carrick this past week.

The 45-year-old was sacked as United head coach on Thursday morning after a disastrous start to the season.

Carrick, who has been replaced by Mauricio Pochettino, oversaw United's worst top-flight start since Ferguson replaced Ron Atkinson 40 years ago - with one victory in 10 Premier League matches as they sit 18th.

Furthermore this season, he only won three of 15 games in all competitions.

According to recent reports, the downturn in the Red Devils' form is bewildering considering their upturn when Carrick replaced Ruben Amorim in mid-January last season. He was handed a two-year contract in May after guiding United to a third-place finish and qualification for the Champions League, losing just two of his 17 games as head coach.

Carrick was sacked as Manchester United head coach on Thursday morning by club chiefs.

He oversaw United's worst top-flight start in Premier League history with one win in 10 games.

Like Carrick, Evans is also out of a job having been part of his backroom staff at United as first-team coach.

After retiring as a player at the end of the 2024-25 season, Evans took up the position of head of loans and pathways at Carrington but left that role last December.

Following Amorim's sacking he returned to the club to help Fletcher during his caretaker manager stint before being kept on by Carrick.

Like Carrick, Evans was relieved of his United duties having been part of his backroom team.

The sole former player still connected directly with the club, Fletcher is their Under 18s head coach. The Scot had to pause his role last season when becoming the club's first-team interim head coach following Amorim's sacking in January - drawing 2-2 with Burnley in the Premier League before overseeing their FA Cup third-round home defeat by Brighton a few days later.

Having come through the club's academy, Fletcher knows what it takes to make the grade at the club and has the likes of Kai Rooney, son of Wayne, and Jacey Carrick, son of Michael, among his squad.

And Fletcher's young charges are enjoying a strong start to the season which has included six goals in wins over Liverpool (6-3) and Burnley (6-0) at the end of last month.

Fletcher is the Red Devils' U18s head coach - nurturing the club's latest crop of rising stars.

The former Red Devils captain had ambitions to go into coaching, having done his badges, but has turned his focus on building up a real estate portfolio - telling Gary Neville on The Overlap last July that he had put £4.5million into building 76 one or two-bedroom apartments in Belgrade, Serbia.

However, this summer it was reported that Vidic had been a previous target of intimidation by a former football chief.

According to Serbian media, encrypted messages show then-Serbia's football president Slavisa Kokeza wanted people to threaten Vidic after he had publicly criticised the Serbian Football Association (FSS) over the national side's failure to qualify for the Euro 2020 tournament.

In the reported devised plot in 2020, Kokeza reportedly told one contact to make it clear to Vidic that he should 'stay away from the association or he will end up in a ditch'.

As well as that, criminals were hired to monitor the former centre-back's movements in Milan, where he lived, and fit his car with a tracking device.

Following the revelations, Vidic and his legal team filed a criminal complaint and sought an investigation into the claimed plot.

'In mid-May, OCCRP and KRIK visited my home and told me they had obtained encrypted messages from Sky ECC (a now-defunct communication encryption service which EUROPOL stated was widely used by criminals and was broken into by European police in 2021) and analysed them,' Vidic told The Athletic in July.

It has been revealed that 'The messages were noted to have come from the then-president of the SFF in 2020. They were about me and how to stop me from talking to the media. At the time, I was commentating on the situation in Serbian football. I was living in Milan, Italy, where I stayed after finishing my career with Inter. I hadn't yet moved back to Serbia, where I am from and where I live.'.

Vidic, who has turned his focus on building up a real estate portfolio, was reportedly a previous target of intimidation by a former football chief.

Van der Sar's calm persona on the football pitch translated well into the boardroom during his near-seven-year stint at Ajax as their chief executive officer.

In a recent development, the former Manchester United goalkeeper joined the Dutch giants' board in 2012, becoming CEO in 2016. During his spell Ajax reached the 2017 Europa League final and 2019 Champions League semi-finals with a young exciting core of players including the likes of Frenkie de Jong and Matthijs de Ligt.

The year Van der Sar left though Ajax finished third that season to qualify for the Europa League play-offs, missing out on the Champions League for the first time since 2009.

A few weeks later in July 2023, Van der Sar was put in intensive care after suffering a brain haemorrhage while on holiday in Croatia.

Three years on since recovering, Van der Sar is enjoying being away from football for the time being telling The Overlap in February: 'Now it's almost three years ago, so I've had time to recover with no stress, no phone in my hand - just doing the stuff that I've wanted to do.

Industry observers note that 'Wake up when you want, walk the dog, go swim in the sea, go on holiday. I went to Latest Zealand for two months with [wife] Annemarie - nice things that I never had the chance to do before.

'I started playing at 18 or 19, finished at 40, and at 41 I became one of the directors at Ajax until 53, so I thought it was the right time to take a step back. That's taken a little bit longer than I originally thought, to be fair, but we are enjoying ourselves very much.'.

Van der Sar was Ajax CEO for seven years before stepping down from the role in 2023.

The ex-goalkeeper is now enjoying life with wife Annemarie after a brain haemorrhage in 2023.

Like Carrick, Van Persie has turned his hand to first-team management since retiring.

His first role was with Dutch outfit Heerenveen - signing a two-year contract with the club ahead of the 2024-25 season. However, his time there lasted just nine months as he took over the reins at Dutch giants Feyenoord.

According to recent reports, however, his time in Rotterdam lasted just 16 months there when he was sacked in June. He had guided them to second in the Eredivisie but they finished 19 points behind champions PSV Eindhoven.

In explaining his sacking, newly-appointed technical director Devy Rigaux cited the style of play as a factor.

Recent findings suggest that 'We conducted a thorough internal analysis,' he noted. 'In this, we took into account, among other things, the development of the style of play and the declining trend in terms of points total, both in Europe and in the Eredivisie.

'The conclusion was that it is better to start the next season with a fresh head coach.'.

The 43-year-old is awaiting a latest job, like Carrick.

Van Persie is at the moment without a managerial job after being sacked by Feyenoord in June.

The sole player from this list to still be playing, Hernandez made history by becoming the first-ever player signed to USL Championship outfit Atletico Dallas.

In July, the 38-year-old penned a two-year deal with an option for a third year at the expansion club which will play in the second-tier of US football, below Major League Soccer.

The Mexican striker still has a few months to wait for his debut though, with the season not beginning until March 2027.

In the meantime, he was part of the FOX broadcast team for the recent World Cup in the United States, Mexico and Canada, serving as an analyst.

Last year, Hernandez was caught up in a sexism storm, which he later apologised for, after he made a series of statements on TikTok 'promoting sexist stereotypes that are considered media violence and go against gender equality in sport'.

Hernandez said women are 'failing' and 'eradicating masculinity'.

'Don't be afraid to be women, to allow yourselves to be led by a man,' said the former Mexico captain on social media.

His remarks sparked a backlash, which led to his apology which included him saying: 'I deeply regret any confusion or discomfort that my recent words have caused.'.

Hernandez was fined and warned about his future conduct.

Hernandez, who attended United's 4-4 draw with Aston Villa on November 8, is the only player still playing and has signed for USL Championship outfit Atletico Dallas ahead of their new term.

Like the majority of the names here, O'Shea's post-playing career has seen him turn to coaching with his current role being the Republic of Ireland assistant head coach.

The 45-year-old has been in this position since August 2024, staying on with his homeland's setup following the appointment of Heimir Hallgrimsson as manager.

In a recent development, O'Shea took charge of the team for four friendly fixtures that year following Stephen Kenny's departure in November 2023. His record read one win, one draw and two defeats in that period.

The former defender will be hoping to help his country qualify for Euro 2028 which will be played on home soil across the Republic of Ireland, England, Scotland and Wales.

O'Shea is Republic of Ireland assistant head coach - a role he has held since August 2024.

Everton appear well ahead of Newcastle United in their preparation for the new Premier League season after a comfortable 3-1 victory at Murrayfield.

On a sobering evening for new Newcastle manager Matthias Jaissle, who changed all 10 outfield players at half-time, Everton’s one and two-touch attacking play proved difficult to contain.

Everton took the lead through Thierno Barry after a defensive error from Sven Botman, before Iliman Ndiaye scored a penalty that was won cheaply by summer signing Hayden Hackney.

Newcastle’s raft of half-time changes helped David Moyes’s team strengthen their grip further, with Tyrique George adding a stylish third and 19-year-old Harrison Armstrong providing his second assist of the game.

Recent findings suggest that among the Newcastle players introduced at half-time was 18-year-old Sean Steur, the exciting midfield prospect signed from Ajax this summer. Aladji Bamba and Bazoumana Toure also flickered with promise, but a sharp start from Jaissle’s team faded.

They pulled a goal back late on when Jacob Murphy’s cross found Harvey Barnes at the back post, but they offered little as an attacking force throughout the second half.

Newcastle have two more friendlies, against Bayer Leverkusen and Strasbourg, before they begin their Premier League season at home to Liverpool.

The club are reeling from the summer departures of Bruno Guimaraes, Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and manager Eddie Howe, but David Hopkinson, the chief executive, struck a bullish tone when he spoke of this being the start of “Newcastle 2.0”.

Everton look the more settled side and club, and the performances of fresh arrivals Hackney and George were encouraging, while Thierno Barry was sharp in the centre-forward position that has proved so difficult for the club to fill in recent seasons.

Everton kick-off their new season at home to Crystal Palace, and keeping Ndiaye at the club beyond the end of the transfer window will be a priority.

Newcastle’s defenders enjoying comfortable possession in the early stages, Everton sitting off in their 4-4-2 defensive shape.

Newcastle get the game under way.

Bagpipes greet the players at Murrayfield, where the pitch has been reconfigured for football. There are only fans in the lower tier, and still plenty of empty seats even so.

Newcastle United manager ​Matthias Jaissle is ‌refusing to dwell on the departure of key players that has left his club in turmoil going into the new season, as they step up their preparations against Everton at Murrayfield this evening.

Jaissle was recruited from Saudi Pro League side Al-Ahli after Eddie Howe left last month, with the German coach joining a club who have lost Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes in quick succession.

“It’s a challenge, a major challenge, always when there’s a transitional period. ‌But it’s ‌not time to ⁠complain, it doesn’t make sense to see the negative things,” Jaissle said.

“We want to see the chance in that situation and that’s our approach from day one. We are here to do our ⁠best job. We want to support the players, the current squad.

“There will be adjustments to see in the coming days, weeks. But for now it’s only focused on the daily work, the work we can influence. That’s all that ​matters now.”.

The 38-year-old coach arrived in Newcastle ‌having won two Austrian Bundesliga titles with Red Bull Salzburg before leading Al-Ahli to back-to-back AFC Champions League crowns.

He remained tight-lipped about upcoming signings.

Sources indicate that “Obviously, in that transition phase, the players who left the club were ‌great ​players, great characters, experienced ⁠players. This is now a vacuum,” he noted.

Sources indicate that “Either we adjust something in the squad, by signing these players, these profiles, or other players ⁠need to step up and fill ​these positions, these leadership roles. I’m quite optimistic, we can work in both scenarios.”.

Jaissle said he had a ​clear vision of how he wants his team to play.

According to recent reports, “The phrase how Newcastle ‌should play like is front-footed, intense, ​aggressive and of course also successful. ​In the end, it’s all about what ⁠I can ⁠say and it’s also why I’m sitting here,” he said.

“The approach we have as a coaching team and the identity of Newcastle is famed for, it’s so linked so close together - which is a perfect fit in my eyes and ​that’s going to be exciting.”.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The Italian had a successful playing career, and he turned to management after retiring, initially starting out with MK Dons.
  • A move to Albion would follow, and Di Matteo would also work for Chelsea, Schalke and Aston Villa, with the high point undoubtedly coming with the Blues, who he won the Champions League and FA Cup with as interim boss.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Roberto Di Matteo has admitted that he was ‘shocked’ West Brom sacked him back in 2011 as they battled to stay in the Premier League.

The Italian had a successful playing career, and he turned to management after retiring, initially starting out with MK Dons.

A move to Albion would follow, and Di Matteo would also work for Chelsea, Schalke and Aston Villa, with the high point undoubtedly coming with the Blues, who he won the Champions League and FA Cup with as interim boss.

Whilst nothing will surpass winning those trophies with Chelsea, Di Matteo really made his name as a manager during his time at The Hawthorns with West Brom.

After making the step up from League One outfit MK Dons, Di Matteo built an Albion side that won promotion to the Premier League in his first season at the club.

They did so by playing a brand of football that the fans really enjoyed, and they carried that into the top flight. Whilst an opening day 6-0 defeat at Chelsea was concerning, the players promptly adapted to the Premier League.

The Baggies had picked up 15 points from their first nine games, which included a memorable 3-2 win at Arsenal, a 2-2 draw at Old Trafford, and they also picked up a point from Tottenham.

So, Albion were performing very well, and they continued the entertaining style of play that had made them such a good watch the season before.

However, that form didn’t continue, and Di Matteo was ultimately dismissed in February, after a miserable period of seven defeats in nine.

And, speaking to Mick McCarthy and Tony Pulis on The Managers podcast, Di Matteo couldn’t hide how disappointed he was at the decision, with Albion outside the relegation zone at the time.

Recent findings suggest that “I was a bit surprised and shocked. We’ve all worked in smaller clubs, so when you have injuries to one or two key players, it’s difficult. Up until the Christmas period we were looking really good, but Jonas Olsson, the centre-back, got injured for a while, and one or two others were not available.

“In the Christmas period, you play every two or three days and you don’t have a deep squad, so you struggle a bit. But, again, we were coming out of it, and I was really shocked.”.

You can understand why Di Matteo was surprised at the decision, as he will have been tasked with keeping the team in the league, and he will argue he was on track to do that.

Plus, this was the first tough spell he had in charge of Albion, so he would’ve hoped that he had enough credit in the bank to be given an opportunity to turn things around.

Yet, football is a ruthless business, and the Albion board needed to make what they felt was the best decision for the club, and the reality is that, in hindsight, it was a call that paid off.

They had been on a terrible run over a period of a few months, and they would say the trend was pointing towards relegation.

West Brom fans, how do you reflect on Roberto Di Matteo's time in charge? Let us know in the comments below.

Industry observers note that as it turns out, West Brom appointed Roy Hodgson, in what was a masterstroke. He kept the team up with ease, and they had another seven consecutive years as a Premier League before relegation in 2018.

Andoni Iraola will hope that his side's attack can make the difference on the weekend, especially as the forwards in the squad struggled in previous games to make an impact.

The likelihood that Liverpool are in the market for a striker is slim considering they not only have Isak in their squad, but also Hugo Ekitike.

While the former may be 27, the latter is only 24, and the club should not be looking to address the number nine spot for years to come.

It would be sensible to recruit younger stars to prepare for any potential decline among first-team stars, but there are great hopes for teenager Will Wright.

Adding yet another centre-forward to the equation would needlessly bloat the squad, and arguably block the pathway of academy talents.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Birmingham City's 2026/27 season has got off to a remarkable start on the pitch, with supporters starting to dream about what might be possible under Chris Davies.

The 41-year-old previously split opinion amongst Blues fans, especially after the way in which the 2025/26 Championship season panned out following continued investment from Knighthead Capital Management.

The club's American investors have vowed to change plenty in such a short space of time, and that doesn't just concern the outlook of Davies' squad in the near future as they chase a Premier League return, but the city of Birmingham as a whole.

Tom Wagner has been heralded for the work he has already put in and what he is planning towards as Blues look to finally realise their potential.

Industry observers note that the idea of looking at the past to move forward can often be frowned upon, but for Wagner and Co. doing exactly that means that Birmingham fans are never likely to lose sight of their identity as the club embarks on a new era.

Last season may have been one of mixed fortunes for Birmingham and their supporters on the pitch, but that didn't mean it wasn't historic in other ways.

Recent findings suggest that indeed, just days before Blues celebrated their 150th anniversary game with a 4-1 rout over Norwich City, the club unveiled the design and name of its upcoming 62,500-seater stadium, which will stand tall less than a mile away from St. Andrew's @ Knighthead Park.

The Powerhouse will pay tribute to the Second City's rich industrial heritage, embodied by its name and design, and that comes across in more ways than one.

The Powerhouse will be the centrepiece of a multi-billion Sports Quarter project that will transform the Bordesley Green area with multiple commercial and retail hubs adjacent to the stadium.

Whilst the chimney-themed design has received major criticism from rival fanbases and beyond, those associated with the club will love how it will repurpose some of Birmingham's rich history.

Over 1,000 bricks which helped structure the City Hospital in Winson Green - built in 1912 as Birmingham Workhouse Infirmary - are being repurposed for the Powerhouse to stand tall on the former site of the Adderley Park Brickworks.

It has been revealed that blues fans, how excited are you to move into the Powerhouse? Comment below!

Sources indicate that city Hospital has been closed since 2024, with the former site making way for a 750-home development adjacent to the Birmingham and Wolverhampton Main Line Canal, approximately 4.1 miles away from St. Andrew's.

"Lovingly salvaged, cleaned, sorted and restored by local experts, the original bricks from Adderley Park Brickworks will be incorporated into the Powerhouse – Birmingham City's future home and a defining part of the city’s Sports Quarter," a section of a statement on Blues' website confirming the purchase of stated bricks read.

In recent months, more work has gone into how the overall Sports Quarter and the Powerhouse stadium will look ahead of a planned opening in the summer of 2031.

Many Blues fans are excited by what is to come, as emotional as it will be when the club have to leave St. Andrew's, having called their current stadium home since the year 1906.

In May, mutiple 'CGI' images were generated and shared by Birmingham's official social media accounts, including how various hospitality packages will be incorporated into the chimney designs.

This includes a high-level view of the pitch which will be named the 'Chimney Seats', as well as 'Restaurant with a View', which will allow guests a view of the city's main skyline, which stands approximately two miles away.

As previously mentioned, Knighthead have certainly done their utmost to embrace themselves in various cultural aspects associated with the West Midlands.

Industry observers note that the Sports Quarter will provide thousands of jobs for locals, whilst also increasing the economy. In the meantime, the investment firm has also acquired stakes in Birmingham Phoenix alongside former Blues academy graduate and Real Madrid star, Jude Bellingham.

The effort which has gone into such a transformative project has not been underestimated by Blues fans, and it has been particularly evident how they feel about Wagner in his recent returns to St. Andrew's after unfortunately suffering a stroke in January.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Sam Varley | 19 Nov 2026 23:57.

Aiming to build a lead at the top of the League One table on the return from the international break, Huddersfield Town will welcome Leicester City to the Accu Stadium on Saturday.

The hosts at the moment lead second-placed Stockport County on goal difference while their visitors sit 11th and four points off the top six.

Huddersfield Town return from the November international break on Saturday aiming to pick up where they left off and pull clear at the top of the League One table.

Aiming to kick on from two disappointing years in England's third tier and fight for promotion back to the Championship, following the permanent appointment of Martin Drury over the summer, they have enjoyed an impressive campaign thus far, currently sitting top having earned 29 points from their first 14 games, winning eight and only losing one of those.

That solitary defeat came in mid-September, and the Terriers have won five and drawn two of seven league outings since, having taken on Luton Town in their final game before the break on the back of four straight victories over Plymouth Argyle, Peterborough United, Wigan Athletic and Bradford City, scoring 11 goals and conceding just two across those.

Drury's men had to settle for a point, though, levelling early in the second half through Joe Taylor in a 1-1 draw before heading into a pair of cup games, firstly bowing out of the FA Cup to fourth-tier Exeter City.

They would then beat Liverpool Under-21s 4-0 in the EFL Trophy last weekend, and now with their full focus back on League One, right now ahead of Stockport County on goal difference and third-placed Oxford United by three points, Huddersfield Town will hope to continue their hot streak and put another victory on the board.

Their visitors, meanwhile, return from the break with their sights set on the playoff places and the hopes of continuing an improved run of their own.

After suffering back-to-back defeats from the Premier League to League One, and turning to Russell Martin in the summer, Leicester City endured another poor start, managing just two wins and nine in their first eight games.

The Foxes appear to have turned a corner since, though, putting three more wins and a draw on the board in their last five league outings to climb into the top half, having beaten Doncaster Rovers, Bromley and Wigan Athletic alongside an away loss to Luton Town.

Martin's men then hosted Stevenage in their final league game before the break and had to settle for a point, having twice led through Sammy Braybrooke and Kamari Doyle and been pegged back, before they recorded consecutive cup victories, getting the better of Oxford City in the FA Cup and Walsall in the EFL Trophy.

Now also focused back on their League One bid, having moved within four points of the playoff spots and five of fourth place, Leicester City will hope to get back to winning ways with the scalp of the league leaders to move closer to the frontrunners on Saturday.

Derensili Sanches Fernandes will return to join him after international duty with Cape Verde, having also shone this season with seven goals and six assists in 14 League One appearances.

Leicester City have a relatively clean bill of health, other than long-term injuries for goalkeeper Jakub Stolarczyk and defender Ben Nelson.

Martin found a somewhat settle starting XI for the most part before the break, and Warren O'Hora, Harry Souttar and Caleb Okoli are bound to continue in a back three with Will Alves and Luke Thomas operating as full-backs.

Will Smallbone, John Lundstram and 18-year-old prospect Louis Page are likely left to compete for two midfield spots, while Sammy Braybrooke and Kamari Doyle may again support front man Emil Riis, who has scored six goals in nine league games so far this term, despite competition from Liam Cullen, Wes Burns and Conor Chaplin.

With Taylor and Sanches Fernandes both in hot streaks, we fancy the Terriers to come out on top at home in a high-quality encounter.

Brian Madjo, 17, electrifies Villa despite Super Cup defeat by PSG

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Unai Emery’s Aston Villa 2.0 remain under construction but from the wreckage of a difficult summer there has emerged a potential star for the future.
  • It has been revealed that emery may have now suffered four successive defeats in the Super Cup, yet the substantial positive from a balmy night in Salzburg was the performance of teenage forward Brian Madjo.
  • Signed from Metz for £10m in January, Madjo had been prevented from playing because of Fifa’s rules on the international transfer of minors.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Unai Emery’s Aston Villa 2.0 remain under construction but from the wreckage of a difficult summer there has emerged a potential star for the future.

It has been revealed that emery may have now suffered four successive defeats in the Super Cup, yet the substantial positive from a balmy night in Salzburg was the performance of teenage forward Brian Madjo. Aged 17 years and 212 days, Madjo became the youngest player to start and score in this continental showpiece, just over a week after he was given permission to play for his club.

Signed from Metz for £10m in January, Madjo had been prevented from playing because of Fifa’s rules on the international transfer of minors. Villa’s appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport to have him registered was upheld on August 4 and what a prospect he appears.

Born in Enfield but raised in Luxembourg, there has been a huge buzz around him since his arrival in the new year.

Paris St-Germain have produced an abundance of talented teenagers over the years and Madjo did not look out of place here.Désiré Doué’s second-half strike secured PSG the Super Cup – contested by the winners of the Champions League and Europa League – for the second successive year, but Emery will have seen enough to give him renewed confidence.

Desire Doue puts PSG 2-1 ahead despite originally being flagged offside 🫣📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/vnMIZCWJaj.

His team played with all the resilience and bravery that has become a trademark, epitomised by the powerful Madjo and another teenager in midfielder George Hemmings.

Sources indicate that emery stated: “Brian has scored goals for us in pre-season and has shown his capacity to work in our idea. I am so happy because the young players were involved in our work and not playing last season.

It has been revealed that “Of course there is still work to do but they highlighted they can play with us. They have responded fantastically and will then feel the confidence. With a loss you can never be happy but overall I am proud of all the players and everything we’ve done. Some changes will be needed but we’re confident.”.

This was a fine Villa performance to silence the doom merchants who have been fearing a troubled season. After the painful sales of Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, Villa are clearly a team in transition. They are operating under restrictions to comply with Uefa’s financial rules and there is still the possibility of another notable player leaving before the transfer deadline day.

Industry observers note that england centre-back Ezri Konsa remains a priority target for Premier League champions Arsenal, and was absent here. Konsa, Emiliano Martínez and Ollie Watkins were all granted extended leave after their participation in the World Cup, which has done little to ease the fears of supporters over more departures. The trio will return to training this weekend.

It has been revealed that while some outsiders are predicting a difficult season for Villa, do not bother telling Emery. He has turned putting noses out of joint into an art form since sweeping into Villa Park and with him around anything feels possible.

The Basque remains optimistic about the future and those hopes will only have been underlined by the performance of Madjo. He bullied PSG centre-back Willian Pacho for much of the evening and even managed to steal the limelight from PSG’s magician Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.

Hemmings, 19, has emerged from the academy and already made a real impression on his manager. Despite the high regard for those youngsters, this always appeared likely to be a tough proposition against a full-strength PSG team. Indeed, before this game in Salzburg only 39 per cent of Europa League winners have beaten their Champions League rivals in this fixture.

The French champions did start slowly, but had been cranking up the pressure before taking a 20th minute lead with a spectacular strike from their Georgian superstar.

Recent findings suggest that what will we learn from the “latest Aston Villa” tonight? After the sales of Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, this is a Villa team in transition.

Sources indicate that I don’t think we can take much from this result tonight, whatever it is. Villa cannot be properly judged until the window closes. Don’t bother telling that to Unai Emery, though. He is ready to continue defying the doubters.

It has been revealed that the Champions League and Europa League winners fight it out in the Uefa Super Cup in Salzburg as PSG take on Aston Villa. PSG took on English opposition in the Super Cup a year ago, when they played Tottenham. PSG fell 2-0 down in that game in Udine but scored two late goals to take it to penalties, where they won 4-3. These sides met in the Champions League knockout stages two seasons ago; PSG did progress from the quarter-final encounter as they went on to win the competition but not without a scare as Aston Villa did win at Villa Park and PSG only progressed 5-4 on aggregate. The two clubs have been involved in a transfer this week, with left-back Lucas Digne re-joining PSG from Aston Villa.

Aston Villa have played in the Super Cup once before back in 1982 when they took in Barcelona. They lost the first leg 1-0 over at Camp Nou but fought back to win the second leg 3-0 at Villa Park to claim the trophy. Aston Villa were last in action out in the Far East last Friday, falling to a 2-1 defeat to Bayern Munich in Hong Kong. It has been a major summer of change at the club, with key starters like Morgan Rogers and Youri Tielemans departing and the likes of Alejandro Garnacho and Joao Gomes arriving.

“I feel like the club is in a newly introduced era, with this possibility to fight for trophies,” Unai Emery told Uefa. “We are trying to be successful through, firstly, [building] a winning team, and then aiming for the positive consequences after it; winning trophies. To play the UEFA Super Cup is another opportunity to be there, the opportunity to win a trophy, to play against Paris Saint-Germain; the [best] team in the world now and another team we can compare [ourselves] with.”.

Emery has confirmed that Ezri Konsa, Ollie Watkins and Emiliano Martinez will not be involved as they are still on their breaks following the World Cup.

PSG have now won back-to-back Champions Leagues, beating Arsenal in the final last season. They have only played a couple of friendlies in pre-season, losing 3-0 to Mallorca before drawing 1-1 against Manchester United. Luis Enrique’s side will take on Lens in the Trophée des Champions on Sunday before kicking off the defence of their Ligue 1 title at home to Rennes.

“I focus on renewing that desire to win again,” Enrique told Uefa. “It is difficult to keep winning. Right now, we have a unique challenge; something that is practically unprecedented in the history of European football, which is to draw level with Real Madrid if we can win a third consecutive Champions League. No-one in history has won three in a row, only Real Madrid. We can equal them. But I do not think there is any team in Europe more motivated than us.

Industry observers note that “No-one rules out PSG any more. Two years ago, it was impossible to put us among the favourites; not impossible, but we were not one of the favourites. Now, no one would say that Paris Saint-Germain are not the favourites. That is something we have earned, but if we are going to maintain that position, we have to work even harder.”.

PSG have added Monaco winger Maghnes Akliouche and Digne to their ranks this summer. They are also pushing to sign Ferran Torres from Barcelona and Mika Godts from Ajax. Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye have both been linked with moves to Liverpool but have been included in their squad for tonight’s game, as have Akliouche and Digne.

It has been a tough few days for Rovers, as the club confirmed that Mowbray had stepped back from his role as head coach due to health challenges.

Many had tipped Blackburn for relegation before a ball was kicked this season, but they have enjoyed a very positive campaign so far under Mowbray, with the team going into the weekend fixtures just three points outside the play-off places.

Therefore, news of Mowbray’s health challenges is a real setback for the club, although it obviously puts football into perspective, with the football world coming together to wish the ex-Middlesbrough chief well.

And, speaking on his Chaz Kicks Off podcast, former Burnley striker Austin echoed those thoughts, and he also explained why the news will unite the Rovers group going into the game.

In a recent development, “When anybody gets ill, or has issues in their personal life, you wish them all the best. But you see from all the players and people that know him, that have made comments, it indicates what kind of bloke he is.

“Blackburn’s teamtalk is done. It’s an easy one to say, let’s win this for the manager, let’s win it for Mowbray. He’s got more notable things going on in his life, which puts football second, but let's go and give everything. Not 110%, but as a collective, let's give 150% and go and run over our neighbours Burnley and make a big statement.

“That’s how I’d see it if I was in the Blackburn dressing room, and it’d be the same if I was a coach or a fan - go and put on a performance for Mowbray.”.

This news came as a shock to the Rovers supporters, so it presumably was the same for the players, and, as Austin says, the initial reaction is to send your thoughts to Mowbray.

But, football will go on, and it’s inevitable that the Blackburn group will want to get results for the manager, as he was a hugely respected figure at the club, and he has personally helped so many of the current squad.

It’s not like they need extra motivation to beat Burnley when you consider the hatred that comes with the East Lancashire derby anyway, but, if they did, then this will provide it, and you can be sure that Mowbray’s name will be spoken about before the players go out on Sunday.

Of course, the coaching staff won’t want to add too much emotional pressure to the players, so they must channel it properly, but the Blackburn squad will head to Turf Moor with full belief that they can pick up three points.

This is a fixture that the Clarets have dominated recently, with Burnley having not lost to their rivals in the last 11 attempts, which is a run that stretches back to 2010.

But, with Burnley’s terrible season so far, and the fact they’ve not won at home in over a year, this is a fantastic chance for Blackburn, and they will hope to make it a special day for the club by winning on Sunday.

The i Paper claim that the Red Devils hold interest in Fulham centre-back Bassey, as well as left-back Robinson.

Bassey has considerable Premier League experience having played 104 Premier League games for Fulham, and the 26-year-old has so far won 64% of his duels this season.

Robinson is capable of playing excellent crosses into the penalty area, and the 29-year-old is much more mobile than Shaw.

While neither are likely to be starters in a team that wins trophies at Old Trafford, the poor physical base of the current squad must be raised, and the duo would elevate the current squad's level.

In order to play in a system as intense as Pochettino's, the players in his squad must be athletic, a quality that Robinson and Bassey share.

However, signing those two players would not address wider imbalances in the team given there are serious concerns about the likes of Lisandro Martinez and Bruno Fernandes.
